articles.description:
Yaas Queen.
The FromSoft-inspired RPG Queen's Domain might have launched in one of the busiest periods of game releases in recent memory, but that's not to say nobody has been picking it up.
Indeed, the game has got off to a rather strong sales start, with developer Freshly Baked and publisher Future Friends confirming that the devilishly difficult indie has already surpassed 300,000 sales across all platforms.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: "We Cannot Believe We Are Reaching Milestones Like This" - Queen's Domain Dev Celebrates Opening Sales

articles.description:
Not that one (but also that one).

Yesterday I finished the Ocarina of Time remake. Having replayed the original over the summer with my kids, we've beansed it through this one, taking our time to enjoy the view and appreciate the myriad changes, but already knowing exactly where to go and what to do.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Opinion: After Finishing Ocarina Of Time, I'm Left Jonesing For A Proper Sequel

articles.description:
Wahoo!
After 13 long years, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out and breaking records left, right, and centre. While folks who only own a Switch or Switch 2 can't get in on the action, we can at least appreciate a good Easter Egg when we see one.
Case in point, the game contains a pretty blatant nod to Mario and Luigi if you know where to look. As highlighted by TheGamingRevolution on YouTube, heading to Lummox County in the north of Leonida and locating a ruined site in the countryside will yield a pair of hats that look remarkably similar to the attire made famous by Nintendo's brotherly mascots.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Random: GTA 6 Hides An Adorable Mario & Luigi Easter Egg In Its Massive World

articles.description:
Company produces custom processor for Switch 2.
Nvidia, one of the largest tech firms in the world and the company responsible for the Switch 2's custom processor, has found itself embroiled in scandal over recent days.
As reported by The Guardian, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, who you might recognise from the 'Creator's Voice Special Edition' video for Switch 2, has now resigned after reported affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and a company employee.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Jensen Huang Has Been Reinstated As Nvidia's President And CEO

articles.description:
Knight's watch.
Sovereign Tower launched on Steam earlier this year and quickly picked up its fair share of fans for its wacky round table management. Today, developer Wild Wits and publisher Curve Games have announced that we Switch fans will be able to get in on the fun in the new year.
That's right, this one is coming to Switch on 14th January 2027. In it, you play as the sovereign of the titular tower, thrust into power after the untimely demise of your predecessor and tasked with keeping the kingdom up and running. To do so, you'll have to recruit knights and match their unique skills to tasks across the land — nabbing stolen manuscripts, taking down evil beings, negotiating with vampires, you know the drill.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Fantasy RPG 'Sovereign Tower' Brings Some Round Table Management To Switch Next Year

articles.description:
Ohh God, the teeth.
Konami has provided zero indication that it plans to bring any Silent Hill games to the Switch 2, so while we wallow in despair, we can at least take comfort in the knowledge that something remarkably similar is on the way.
Revealed at The Horror Game Awards 2026, Ugly Within is published by Serafini Productions and confirmed for Switch 2, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. There's no release date as of yet, but judging from the quality of the trailer, it seems development is proceeding well.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Unsettling Silent Hill-Inspired Horror Game Confirmed For Switch 2

articles.description:
A weekend of review bombing.
The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was one of a handful of games brave enough to launch on 'GTA Day' last week, but while Rockstar has been swimming in positive reception ever since, Isaac's re-release hasn't been so lucky.
Indeed, the game has been subject to a hefty review bombing from players on Steam after it was discovered that AI-generated music was used in the release's new GTA 6-themed online mode (thanks for the heads up, Steam Hype).
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: "Woke Up To A S**t Show" - Binding Of Isaac Dev Shocked To Find GenAI Music In 'Repentance+'

articles.description:
One of 2027's big-hitters.
New details regarding Kirby and the World Beyond have been revealed via Nintendo's winter catalogue in Japan (via Genki_JPN on X). While hardly comprehensive, it provides a little more insight into the game's story along with the abilities and environments available upon its release.
Of course, we know from the debut trailer that this will boast a much broader world than The Forgotten Land, with one detail noting how you can use Kirby's abilities to explore at your own pace. We also get a touch more context behind King Dedede's role, with the article stating that "a mysterious girl" has been kidnapped by the antagonist.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Kirby And The World Beyond Details Revealed In Nintendo Catalogue

articles.description:
Passing the torch.
Let's see what's in the box
The Treasure Chest
A few weeks ago, my brother sent me a photo with zero context. He was at our parents’ house, helping them pack up for a cross-country move, when he found something unusual: a heavy metal box with a latch.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Feature: A Lost Box Restored My Faith In Zelda's Staying Power

articles.description:
Issue #42 - November 2026.
Hello, you. Yes, you. It's just us here today - everyone else is busy in Hyrule or Leonida right now.
In fact, it's been like that for most of the month, it seems, as the Nintendo Life Mailbox is looking pretty empty! So, it'll be a nice quick one this month. We'll have you back with your preferred ride — equine or automotive — in a jiffy.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Mailbox: Ocarina Intruders, Pikmin Day, Too Many Humans - Nintendo Life Letters

articles.description:
One good, one Fawful?
Ahoy folks, and welcome to another edition of Box Art Brawl!
Looking back on last week, we checked out Dr. Mario & Puzzle League for the GBA to celebrate its recent addition to the NSO library. Neither design in this instance was particularly enthralling, and this is perhaps evident in the final result. Japan just about managed to claim a win with 51% of the vote, with North America / Europe making up the remaining 49%. Oof, so close!
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Poll: Which Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga Box Art Is The Best?

articles.description:
The producer's pick 'Pangoro' missed out.

Famous Japanese game director and producer Katsuhiro Harada, known for the Bandai Namco series Tekken, has revealed a Pokémon he wanted to add to the Pokémon fighting game Pokken Tournament but it didn't make the cut.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Katsuhiro Harada Reveals The Pokémon He Wanted To Add To Pokken Tournament

articles.description:
Reminder: The Fatal Fury movie antagonist is now available.
:
SNK's expansion of the Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves roster will continue with the release of Laocorn next week on 19th November 2026.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Fatal Fury: City Of The Wolves Adds Laocorn From The Motion Picture

articles.description:
Pauline when?
: We understand GTA 6 is a big deal, but Build-A-Bear Workshop has also teased some important news this week.
On its official Instagram page, the store where you build your own bear, has announced it's "going bananas" for its newest furry friend, who is "coming soon from the jungle". As you can see, it's a silhouette of Donkey Kong!
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: "We're Going Bananas For Our Newest Furry Friend" - Donkey Kong Out Now On Build-A-Bear Workshop

articles.description:
SWiitching it up.
Many people reading this will have a Wii in the house. Even if it's collecting dust in the cupboard after launching 20 years ago, there's over 100 million of the things out in the wild, so the chances are that you or your family have access to one somewhere.
However, on the off-chance you don't have a Wii to hand — or you sold it years ago to save three DVDs' worth of space — don't fret. While the system has a selection of exclusives you can't easily play elsewhere, many Wii games have come to Switch in HD remastered form over the years.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Feature: Don't Have Your Wii Set Up? Here Are 20 Wii Games You Can Play On Switch

articles.description:
GT, Ay?
Pretty quiet week in the world of video games, eh? Nothing particularly groundbreaking released that we can think of...
Oh wait! Yes, that Grand Theft Auto 6 launched, didn't it? And it was a rather big deal. The game shot to the top of Metacritic's all-time best games list (tied with the original Ocarina of Time), and Digital Foundry weighed in on whether it'll ever come to Switch 2.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (21st November)

articles.description:
He's apparently still working at "full throttle".
As we reflect on 25 years of Super Smash Bros. Melee, it seems game director Masahiro Sakurai is taking a moment to remind everyone that Kirby Air Riders has now been available for a year.
As highlighted by Sakurai on social media, the Switch 2 exclusive is officially one year old as of this week. It's received multiple updates since launch and Nintendo recently rolled out the last two amiibo.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Sakurai Celebrates Kirby Air Riders' First Anniversary And Seemingly Ponders His Future As A Game Creator

articles.description:
Your companion to a huge adventure.
Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.
That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Guide: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

articles.description:
GTA 6 fans are reportedly review bombing the game.

It's been a huge year for the games industry with all sorts of heavy-hitters releasing over the past few months, and as we look towards the end of 2026, we're now checking in on Metacritic's highest-rated games of the year based on the user score.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Ocarina Remake's 'Positive' User Review Score Is Now Under Fire

articles.description:
Update: It's now "estimated" to release later this month.
: Telltale Games has announced the Nintendo Switch version of The Wolf Among Us Remastered "needs a little bit more time".
In an official statement shared on social media, it mentions how this remaster starring Sheriff Bigby Wolf will "launch as planned on October 29 for PlayStation, Xbox, and PC", and the "Nintendo Switch version will follow at a later date".
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered Has Been Delayed For Switch

articles.description:
NSO release when?
One first-party title from the GameCube library that's well and truly outlived this particular Nintendo generation is Super Smash Bros. Melee, and today happens to be the game's 25th anniversary in Japan.
After introducing fans to the series in 1999 on the N64, Masahiro Sakurai and the team at HAL Laboratory & Nintendo rolled out this new, improved, and faster take on the all-star Nintendo fighter in November 2001. Not only was it a popular couch game, but Melee went on to have an incredibly successful run as a competitive game.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Anniversary: Super Smash Bros. Melee Has Now Been Duking It Out For 25 Years

articles.description:
A'ight, slow down.
There's been a lot of talk around how long GTA fans have been waiting for the latest entry to launch, but Persona isn't actually that far behind. Persona 5 – in its original state – released over a decade ago on 15th September 2016, and although Persona 6 has now been officially announced, we're none the wiser as to when it will actually come out.
It's likely to finally land at some point in 2027 after the dust has settled from Persona 4 Revival, but according to a recent interview with general producer Kazuhisa Wada (thanks, Nintendo Everything), fans won't have to wait quite so long for the inevitable Persona 7.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Persona 6 Doesn't Have A Date Yet, But Atlus Says You Won't Have To Wait As Long For Persona 7

articles.description:
And you'll need to pass the criteria to register interest.
We've been keeping an eye out for news of Nintendo's playable and electric ocarinas going on sale in Europe for a good while now. It looks like sales are just around the corner, but you're going to need to jump through some hoops if you want to get your hands on one.
Both the Nintendo playable model and HORI electric version will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. You can register your interest in getting either model now on the Nintendo website, but there are some criteria that you'll have to pass first.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Zelda Playable & Electric Ocarinas Will Initially Be Sold On An Invite-Only Basis (Europe)

articles.description:
Sweet Temtemptations.
Crema Games' Temtem was one of the better Pokémon-likes we had played when it arrived on Switch back in 2022. The dev released its final update a couple of years back, but soon, we'll get a chance to play its Survivors-style spinoff.
Temtem: Swarm launches on Switch on 21st January 2027 after coming to Steam back in April. An initial glance made us think this was Crema's take on Pokémon Unite, but on closer inspection, it's far more Vampire Survivors.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Pokémon-Like Temtem's Bullet Heaven Spin-Off Arrives On Switch Next Year

articles.description:
Every game we scored 9/10 or higher, plus a personal pick.
With Nintendo launching its Black Friday sale on the European eShop earlier this week, we knew it was only a matter of time before our friends in North America got some savings of their own. And what do you know, they have!
Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' sale is now live on the North American storefront, with discounts across a bunch of first- and third-party delights. It'll be sticking around until 2nd December at 11:59pm PT, so you still have a couple of weeks to make the most of it.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
articles.title: Guide: 43 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' eShop Sale (US)

articles.description:
Prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a new version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO Series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.
  
Read more
articles.title: 28 years later, grizzled XCOM-style WW2 tactics game Soldiers at War gets a fresh tour of duty on modern PCs

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Ho ho ho, the RPS Advent Calendar 2026 is... not ready yet. We haven’t written the words, and I keep forgetting to unblur that new picture of Horace (drawn by the reliably talented Amanda Flagg). But while drag our lumpen feet on the business of deciding our favourite games this year, RPS readers have begun plotting, and scheming, and apparently in some cases, spreadsheeting. That’s right: the Advent Calendar Guessing Game has returned, and is open right now for keen participants.
Read more
articles.title: Think you know games? That we liked? This year? Then join the RPS Advent Calendar Guessing Game 2026

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Literal decades ago, I tried to make a first-person RPG in HyperCard. I got as far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for the shareware version. I mention this because new, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.
This risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.
 Read more
articles.title: Might and Magic meets, er, paper in sunny new RPG Rise of Furax, a turn-based island tale that is entirely drawn by hand

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.
Read more
articles.title: "Don't let this happen again": GTA 6 hacker who pleaded guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach released under supervision

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's important questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.
 Read more
articles.title: Finally, some former Valorant and Sky devs have answered the call for a Peak-style platformer about throwing a cat through a hole in spacetime

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Fine Monday to ya, reader. In the interest of allowing Edwin more time to spend with his interview transcripts, you’ve got me on Maw duty this week. Not much chance of it going ungorged, in any case – while the continued bellows of Grand Theft Auto VI have frightened away most of the air-quotes "big" games from this late November habitat, many others remain, undaunted. Or because they probably thought the Venn diagram of GTA fans and grand strategy expansion fans was just two rings.
There’s still some Vice City-adjacent matters we’ll be covering this week – chief among them the Rockstar North unionisation vote, which is set to close in the coming days – but as I said to Edwin and Mark this morning, the cool thing about the continued lack of a PC version is that it leaves open a space to be filled with other things. Judging by what’s out this week, there’s certainly no shortage to choose from.
Read more
articles.title: This week in PC games: Raise a psychedelic baby, invent terrible new religions, and run your own PC hardware business

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Yep, he's back. Less than two weeks after Jensen Huang resigned from being CEO of Nvidia following reports of multiple affairs, the company's board have reinstated him "effective immediately".
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following alleged affairs, as US government support renders 'please give me my job back, go USA' a highly persuasive plea

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.


In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.
 
Read more
articles.title: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
An update for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently announced the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.
Read more
articles.title: Undisclosed AI-generated music pulled from The Binding of Isaac Repentance+ update, as attempt to get satirical on GTA 6 launch day goes awry

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Sundays are for googling local purveyors of live Christmas trees, the sole upside of no longer having a cat being that you can once again enjoy the smell of chopped woodland without the risk of it poisoning a family member. Well, then again, I mean... empirically speaking, you're probably just assuming that your human loved ones haven't eaten spruce needles. Can you say for an absolute fact that they wouldn't?
Fortunately, while your nan is off having her stomach pumped, you can pass the time by reading some good words from this week.
Read more
articles.title: The Sunday Papers

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.
 
Read more
articles.title: Alt Video is a digital, faux Blockbuster video store that you can fill with movies from your Letterboxd watchlist and Plex server

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own shows through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.
 
Read more
articles.title: Public-access television is born anew in NIGHT EYE TV, a digital goggle box filled with art game curios

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Oh I do love an eldritch horror creature, I do, especially one that at first glance may only be slightly different from what I'm used to seeing. Eldritch Empathy, then, seems like a grand ole game to satisfy my wanton need to experience such things. It's a puzzle roguelite that isn't exactly a Papers Please-like but certainly feels reminiscent of one, where you have to "analyse corrupted creatures, purify their emotions and learn how to communicate with an eldritch being."
 
Read more
articles.title: Eldritch Empathy is a Papers Please-esque roguelite about diagnosing cosmic horror creatures and trying not to lose your marbles as you do

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person. It was probably a wise choice on his part, obfuscating his current appearance with everyone's favourite annoying dog, essentially never speaking aloud in livestreams and instead using a text-to-speech bot, and posting only when there's notable enough Deltarune updates of if it would be very funny. But as it turns out, that sense of mystery extends to the team that's making Deltarune too, as Fox won't tell his devs how the game ends until they've built enough of it.
 
Read more
articles.title: "Everyone agrees it's more fun this way": Toby Fox won't tell his team how Deltarune ends until they've built enough of it

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel. No, in fact the next bit of DLC for Darkest Dungeon 2 was teased only a couple of weeks ago, with a new trailer shared today actually showing off what it's all about.
 
Read more
articles.title: Darkest Dungeon 2's next bit of DLC is a short run, combat focused gauntlet where you must do everything in your power to please the audience

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Terrible news, readers. Not only have several members of the Treehouse abandoned us, citing flimsy excuses like "James, you remember I've got that holiday booked, right?," many that remain have forsaken their duties and are playing something called a Play Station. What, all those Not GTA retrospectives we ran this week not inspiring enough for you? Can't even wait an indeterminate amount of time for a completely unconfirmed PC port? For what, some silly little cultural event of staggeringly vast and likely medium-altering importance? Whatever, was still made with union busting. Allegedly.
On the plus side, all the absences this week does mean the perfidy can be done and dusted quickly. Here's what we're playing this weekend:
Read more
articles.title: What are we all playing this weekend?

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.
Read more
articles.title: Nvidia's latest graphics card driver appears to be unnecessarily writing to PC SSDs, something that's dumb, annoying and definitely warrants reverting

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.
However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.
We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.
Read more
articles.title: Vote now for 2026's RPS 100: Reader Edition

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.
Read more
articles.title: Akira Kurabayashi, company director at Arika and developer on Street Fighter EX, Tetris 99, Fighting EX Layer and more, has sadly passed away due to heart failure

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".
Read more
articles.title: Amid a year of layoffs, Ubisoft yank the cover off Motherbrain, their new studio "focused on AI for gameplay innovation"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Cyberleek, the GTA 6 leaker or leakers who shared a bunch of alleged gameplay earlier this year, are now claiming to have released a nearly complete in-development build of the crimsim's Xbox version. Continuing their established grift, the leaker or leakers are threatening to release the main executable file they've withheld unless people pump up the value of their cryptocurrency.
Read more
articles.title: GTA 6 leaker claims to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of Rockstar's crimsim onto the net, shouts that the "community will have it emulated inside a week"

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.
Read more
articles.title: Valve are pausing Steam Machine 2TB orders over "supply constraints," though the 512GB model is free of its waitlist

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.
Read more
articles.title: Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be important or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has launched on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere."
 
Read more
articles.title: Ignore that other game about crime that's out and burgle some ugly farmhouses in Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" with a 2000s Cartoon Network vibe

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada. Both studios affected, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, had a hand in last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows, with Montreal especially being a major and long-tenured development hub for the company.
Read more
articles.title: Ubisoft lay off 166 more staff, this time at their Montreal and Quebec City studios, while mumbling about "current production priorities and business needs"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Epic Games are, as you're probably aware, going big on genAI at the moment. To the extent that, last month, the Tim Sweeney-helmed company announced the Epic AI MegaJam. Build a playable game in Unreal Engine or Unreal Editor for Fortnite with help from as many AI agents or tools as you like was the pitch.
So, naturally, sorting the submissions by 'Popular' turns up a game about a fish with a sniper rifle whose creator says they deliberately made it without using any generative AI.
Read more
articles.title: Fish with a sniper rifle takes aim at Tim Sweeney's hopes and dreams, as genAI-free meme game tops Epic Games' vibe-coding megajam

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.
Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.
 Read more
articles.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world

articles.author: Jeremy Laird
articles.description:
Your next gaming monitor should be an OLED display. There, I've said it. And I know the notion won't please everyone. After all, a large grey proboscidean lumbers into the room whenever OLED technology is mentioned. Put simply, almost any risk of the dreaded burn-in is an immediate deal-breaker for some. I do get that.
Likewise, despite my musings just the other day on how affordable gaming monitors have generally become and the fact you can now snag an OLED panel, specifically, for sub £300 / $300, it's a stretch to say OLED gaming comes cheap. And yet here I am arguing firmly in favour of OLED.
Read more
articles.title: They're more complicated and more expensive than LCD screens, but your next gaming monitor should still be an OLED

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Try not to get whole armies of Space Marines pasted against the surfaces of planets thanks to your shoddy tactics, please. So ask the bosses of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, who're keen not to have their training workloads doubled because you're a crap general and have gotten a tight-knit force of uber-tough grunts killed unnecessarily, hope as they watch you play. This and other things have been emphasised by a fresh stream showing off over an hour of campaigning in the strategy warhammerer.
Read more
articles.title: Hour-long Total War: Warhammer 40,000 campaign stream shows off ship battle-less fleet management, makes clear how not ideal getting Space Marine armies killed is

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The employment tribunal over Rockstar's firing of 34 workers last year has come to an end for now, pending a final verdict from the judge. Said judge hasn't offered a concrete estimate of when her judgement will arrive, but has reportedly asserted that she'll provide it "as quickly as [she] possibly can".
Read more
articles.title: Rockstar firings tribunal hears closing statements, with judge promising to deliver a verdict "as quickly as I possibly can" - though it may take a while

articles.author: Max Moser
articles.description:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth, the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.
Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.
Read more
articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!


Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.
  
Read more
articles.title: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Funky feudal family frolic Crusader Kings 3 got its second major expansion of the year this week. It's called Silk and Silver (read my impressions), is all about merchant republics, and shipped alongside a beefy free update to the base game which - while largely focused on overhauling economics - also has some funny patch notes and features worth being aware of.
Read more
articles.title: "Abducting your own lover no longer gives you opinion of yourself" declare the notes for Crusader Kings 3's free Florin update, released alongside Silk and Silver

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.
A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.
You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.
Read more
articles.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.
In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."
 Read more
articles.title: "It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 launches on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
In a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.
Read more
articles.title: SteamDB will add "affiliate links to authorised game retailers" and a new tab dedicated to mods, first update since Nexus Mods takeover confirms

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.
 Read more
articles.title: Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.
The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.
Read more
articles.title: PC remains GTA 6's last hope for 60fps smoothness as Rockstar confirm such an option isn't coming to even the swankiest consoles

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.
 Read more
articles.title: Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.
Read more
articles.title: Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.
 
Read more
articles.title: Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.
 
Read more
articles.title: The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.
 
Read more
articles.title: Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!
 
Read more
articles.title: Archetype go all in on the Mass Effect vibes with a FemJun reveal, but I'm just left hoping they'll call the alternative option MascJun to balance it out

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.
It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.
 Read more
articles.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.
 
Read more
articles.title: Only two days out from GTA 6, its publisher Take-Two lay off staff at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.
Read more
articles.title: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Update 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:
The original article continues below.
As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.
Read more
articles.title: Embracer begin yet another round of layoffs at Crystal Dynamics, while they're still midway through development on two Tomb Raider games

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest update post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.
Read more
articles.title: Former Dishonored designer joins the team on New Blood's Victorian immersive sim Gloomwood, with a new level and new weapons coming this year

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
For absolutely no reason whatsoever, I’ve recently fired Sleeping Dogs up again. The United Front Games-developed, Square Enix-published open-world crime romp is still as good as it’s always been, and still occupies its own corner in the dingy bar where the GTAs and GTA-likes hang out. Back in 2015, RPS co-founderman Alec Meer (RPS in peace) referred to it as “the halfway house between GTA's sneering arrogance and Saints Row's chaotic nonchalance”. Fair enough, I’ve never been that big a Saints Row guy, but I see slumbering canines a bit differently.
Read more
articles.title: I'm not saying Sleeping Dogs is the world's best life of crime sim, but no other game has replicated the importance of pork buns to whole manhood as deftly

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.
The manifesto states that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.
Read more
articles.title: "Games are best made by people": The IWGB and other European unions publish joint manifesto calling on workers, employers and consumers to reject genAI

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that plan release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the company has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental issues.
Read more
articles.title: Unity launches new Fellowship program, offering a "no recoup" $50,000 grant to indie developers planning to launch their game in the next 12 months

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.


The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.
 
Read more
articles.title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

articles.author: Ashley Schofield
articles.description:
Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.
Read more
articles.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer will get local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027 with new 'Free Play' mode, finally letting racers yell at one another in a tangible space

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.
Read more
articles.title: Judge denies motion to dismiss lawsuit accusing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron of worsening RAM crisis by fixing memory prices and supply

articles.author: J.D. Harlock
articles.description:
PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.
Read more
articles.title: Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.


Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.
 
Read more
articles.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.
I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.
Read more
articles.title: My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be announced, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a new GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.
Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.
Read more
articles.title: Each new GTA moves the series closer and closer to the original Mafia, the open-world game that bettered Rockstar

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.
All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".
 Read more
articles.title: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.
Read more
articles.title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach which the company claim cost them $5 million

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Happy this week, all! Please throw yourself upon the floor in consternation, clawing at your face and hair, for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is nigh. In just a few short days, every gaming vertical under the sun will be publishing features about the exact depth of Jason Duval's ripped abs and what this Says About America Today, or how many bottle caps you must gather to unlock Lucia Caminos' Gundam mode.
Fortunately for my sanity, Rockstar's crime colossus isn't yet nigh on PC, though the word is that modders driven nuts by Claude will soon be along with an unofficial "port". As such, while we do have a few Grandiosely Thievish articles in store this week – not least, coverage of the on-going unionisation situation at Rockstar – we can afford to spend a few hours writing about non-GTA things. The appraisal of mushrooms, for example, or the solubility of rubber hosing, or the parrying of spells. Without further ado, here's this week's uncommonly flavourful crop of new PC games. Don't worry, dear Maw. You'll get to eat Jason eventually.
 Read more
articles.title: This week in PC games: start a new life in Vice City, escape a dying universe before the last black hole evaporates, and avenge your pigeon with a sledgehammer

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.
Read more
articles.title: "Nobody was hurt" in shooting near Clockwork Revolution devs InXile Entertainment's office, the Xbox-owned studio and police confirm

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".
Read more
articles.title: "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.
Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?
 Read more
articles.title: The Sunday Papers

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.
 
Read more
articles.title: Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access.
 
Read more
articles.title: Rasen, out in early access now, is a PvP focused take on Dark Souls that borrows one of fighting games' best techy tricks

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.
 
Read more
articles.title: Congratulations to people who feel mean shooting random NPCs, because GTA 6 tries "to provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.
 
Read more
articles.title: From 2D to 3D and back to 2D again, the original platforming classic Super Meat Boy returns with a slick remaster complete with new levels and too many old saws

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a new game plus mode.
 
Read more
articles.title: Missed something on your first go around The Blood of Dawnwalker? I've got good news, as next week's update adds in new game plus

articles.author: Julian Benson
articles.description:
Ah, yes, Saturday. Traditionally a day for relaxing. Why is it then I'm packing, doing last-minute shopping, and going to a wedding all in the space of eight hours? Because, Julian, you are a fool who, as ever, has left everything far too late.
What about the team, though. I imagine they've managed their time much better.
Read more
articles.title: What are we all playing this weekend?

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each update may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.
 
Read more
articles.title: Cyberpunk trading sim Probably Stolen is getting three big updates with new starting scenarios - organ trading, junk empires and fine dining

articles.author: James Archer
articles.description:
Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.
Read more
articles.title: While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
What's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more important laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.
I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.
 
Read more
articles.title: Worst Class Ever takes asymmetrical multiplayer back to school, with a teacher player trying to spot the naughty children among the NPCs

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have announced plans to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.
Read more
articles.title: Crusader Kings publishers Paradox announce CEO swap, say they're "in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges"

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.


When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.
 
Read more
articles.title: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.
Read more
articles.title: Microsoft suffer system outage affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot, exec says there's "no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity"

articles.author: Edwin Evans-Thirlwell
articles.description:
Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!"
But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.
 Read more
articles.title: Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes

articles.author: Mark Warren
articles.description:
Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.
"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.
Read more
articles.title: Wolfenstein 3 and new id Software game confirmed, as Xbox boss somehow unrelatedly shouts about one person soon wielding "capabilities that once required entire nations"

articles.author: Oisin Kuhnke
articles.description:
Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."
 
Read more
